description:
Command aliases are extra names for Wynem's commands that only work in your server. They let you shorten the commands your server uses most, or name them in a way that suits your community.

An alias works exactly like the name it points to. You can point an alias at a command's main name or at one of its built-in aliases, and it keeps that alias's behaviour. For example, an alias pointing at `bottomcaption` puts the caption at the bottom, just like `e!bottomcaption` does.
Command aliases only apply to prefix commands. Server aliases for a command are also listed when viewing that command with <command:help [command]|help command:[command]>.

tabs.name: Adding an alias
content: To add a command alias, use the <command:addcommandalias [command] [alias]|botconfig commandaliases add command:[command] alias:[alias]> command.
For example: <command:addcommandalias bottomcaption bc|botconfig commandaliases add command:bottomcaption alias:bc>

data.title: Command alias added
data.description: You can now use `e!bc` to run `e!bottomcaption`

content:
Aliases can only contain letters, numbers, `-` and `_`.

An alias can take over the name of one of Wynem's commands or aliases, so you can change what that name does in your server. A few names are reserved and cannot be used, such as `help` and the command alias commands themselves. Aliases also cannot use the name of one of the server's custom commands.
Adding an alias that already exists replaces it, pointing it at the new command instead.

data.title: Command alias updated
data.description: You can now use `e!bc` to run `e!caption`

tabs.name: Viewing aliases
content: To view all the command aliases in the server, use the <command:viewcommandaliases|botconfig commandaliases view> command.

tabs.name: Removing an alias
content: To remove a command alias, use the <command:removecommandalias [alias]|botconfig commandaliases remove alias:[alias]> command.
For example: <command:removecommandalias bc|botconfig commandaliases remove alias:bc>

description: If the server later adds a custom command with the same name as one of its aliases, the custom command takes priority over the alias.
